stage_a.note: He is very energetic, confident, and highly engaged throughout the pitch while removing his layers.
He enthusiastically throws off his outer garments and speaks loudly with great animation.
He is approachable and friendly, though his delivery is mostly focused on the performance itself.

venture.description: Extreme cold weather clothing designed to keep the wearer warm even when wet, using proprietary insulation technology.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Dale introduces himself and his company, seeking $600k for 15%, and explains the problem with cold weather clothing.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Dale asks Skyler to report the temperature in the cryo tank.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Skyler reports the temperature is negative 112 Fahrenheit to prove the product's capability.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Lori laughs at the extreme temperature mentioned in the cryo tank.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Dale invites Robert to experience the technology since he had been in a cryo tank before.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Robert expresses his eagerness to try the cryo tank.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Lori encourages Robert to get into the tank.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Dale directs attention back to the clothing samples they brought.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin jokes about cranking the temperature down to 250 below zero.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Skyler adjusts the settings on the cryo tank.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Dale hands out special prototype winter gloves to Lori and Kevin.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Lori admires the hoodie that was handed to her.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Dale hands a parka and snowmobile gloves to Mark.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Robert asks Dale what specific garment he is currently wearing.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Dale explains he is wearing the base layer.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Lori compliments the sleek look of the base layer Dale is wearing.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Dale notes the base layer is comfortable from 70 degrees down to minus 10.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Robert announces he is ready to enter the tank.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Barbara asks if Robert is wearing the same base layer as Dale.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Dale confirms and explains it is typically worn next to the skin.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Lori playfully flexes while examining the clothing.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin urges them to put Robert into the cryo tank.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Robert steps into the freezing cryo tank.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin jokes again about lowering the temperature to 300 below.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Dale explains that the longer the door is shut, the colder it gets.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Lori playfully tells them to hit Robert with more cold.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Dale reassures them that the tank uses safe oxygen.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Mark laughs at Robert's situation in the tank.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Robert stands inside the freezing tank.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin laughs at Robert enduring the cold.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Dale asks Robert how his hands feel in the cold.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Robert exits the cryo tank after the test.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin laughs as Robert gets out of the tank.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Dale resumes his pitch, questioning who his target market should be.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Lori asks Robert how he felt; Robert says his toes were freezing but his top was fine.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Dale emphasizes that Robert feeling nothing on top is incredible.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Dale highlights their proprietary disruptive insulation technology found in all their products.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin asks who they are targeting as their primary market.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Dale explains he needs an influencer and distribution channels.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin asks what their historical sales figures are.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Dale states they have sold 3.5 million dollars since 2012.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin points out that 3.5 million over 7 years is not a lot.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Robert clarifies that Dale has been working on this for 7 years.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Lori asks for their sales figures over the last 12 months.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Dale replies that they did 407,000 dollars in 2018.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Dale explains they had great growth until oil prices dropped, which devastated their industrial sales.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin confirms that industrial clients in the oil patch were their primary market.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Dale confirms, noting there was a lot of opportunity there.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Lori asks how they differentiate from competitors if they enter the retail market.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Dale states their value proposition is keeping people warm even when soaking wet.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin asks why the clothing is warm and how it solves the wetness problem.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Dale deflects by describing a scenario of falling through ice while fishing.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Dale shows a video of himself jumping into freezing water to demonstrate the gear.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Lori asks if Dale is a scientist and inquires about his background.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Dale explains he is a serial entrepreneur who experienced three colossal failures and seven years of famine.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Lori asks if he really has eight children.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Dale jokes that having eight kids would make him cry too.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Dale mentions that his fourth venture was a massive success.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin questions how he failed three times before finding magic on the fourth try.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Dale explains he built a telecommunications company to 33 million and retired at 40.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin challenges Dale, saying his strategy and target market are completely undefined.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Dale tries to interject and disagree with Kevin's assessment.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin argues that Dale is competing with mega marketers in fashion while selling to oil workers.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Dale explains he is looking for low-hanging fruit and views the Sharks as influencers.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Lori agrees with Kevin that Dale lacks a defined market.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Dale states they will continue targeting industrial workers and outdoorsmen.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Robert asks if Dale considered licensing the patented technology to clothing manufacturers.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Dale says they tried but were rejected because the tech was unproven, leading them to create Fortress.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin compliments the look of the base layer, saying he would wear it skiing in St. Moritz.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Dale points out that Kevin would still need to wear his outer shell of choice over it.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Robert asks why he cannot simply wear the base layer alone to go skiing.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Dale explains the base layer lacks a wind stopper and functions like insulated thermal underwear.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Lori exits, stating she is confused by the market positioning and the need for an outer shell.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Dale expresses hope that Lori might reconsider and come back in later.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Lori laughs at Dale's optimism about her returning.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Barbara suggests Dale position the company strictly as an underwear brand.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Dale says he is open to positioning the brand as an underwear company.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Barbara exits, stating the idea came too late and she lacks the energy to build a new business.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin exits, citing a lack of marketing focus and an undefined strategy for his investment.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Robert exits, explaining that the confusing message between oil workers and ice fishing is too much.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Dale expresses his desire to get the investors excited about the product.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Mark exits, stating Dale is drowning in too many opportunities and lacks a single focused niche.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Dale thanks Mark for his time and feedback.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Mark advises Dale that selling technology requires a clean, simple message rather than bouncing between categories.

decisions.note: Confused about how the product beats the market and the disconnect of wearing a shell on top.
Suggests positioning as underwear, but says it came too late and she lacks the energy to build a whole new business.
Missing focus on marketing and strategy; hard to part with $600k to test ideas.
The message is too confusing, jumping between oil workers and ice fishing.
Drowning in opportunity; too many categories instead of focusing on one niche.
